case.title: Payment Sent
case.brief: Daniel is selling his bike for $400. The buyer, Kofi, is outside, says he has already paid, and sends a screenshot as proof. He wants to ride off right now. Daniel's gut says something's off.

evidence.title: Kofi → Daniel
evidence.body: Sent! Screenshot attached, it shows completed. I'm outside, parking is limited, bring the bike down quick.

evidence.title: Screenshot attached to the 14:08 message
evidence.body: Banking app screen. 'Transfer Completed'. $400.00 to Daniel Okora. Ref: TX-48210937. Time: 14:05. The phone's status bar clock reads 14:41.

evidence.title: Daniel's incoming transfers
evidence.body: No incoming transfers. Last credit: $62.00 on Tuesday. Real earlier receipt: 'Ref: TX-5520184736'.

evidence.title: Bank notice
evidence.body: Instant transfers arrive within 60 seconds. Transfer references are 'TX-' followed by 10 digits. A screenshot is not proof of payment.

evidence.title: The listing
evidence.body: Road bike, $400, price firm. Posted 3 days ago, 11 enquiries, 2 offers below asking.

options: It's pending and will arrive soon

questions.q: How many separate inconsistencies does the screenshot contain?
What should Daniel do before handing over the bike?
options: Hand it over, since the screenshot says completed
Wait until the money shows in his own bank account
Let Kofi take it and settle later
Ask Kofi to re-send the screenshot

case.explanation: Instant transfers land within 60 seconds, yet Daniel's account shows nothing between 14:00 and 14:50, so no money arrived. The screenshot has three flaws: the name is 'Okora', not 'Okoro'; the reference has 8 digits instead of the bank's 10; and the status-bar clock reads 14:41 on a screenshot sent at 14:08. The amount, $400, matches the asking price, so it isn't a flaw. A screenshot proves nothing, so Daniel should wait until the funds appear in his own account.

meta.theme: marketplace scam with a forged payment screenshot
